title: The First Declension — Feminine in η
subtitle: ἡ ἀρετή, ἡ τιμή, ἡ τέχνη — the most regular type.
objectives: Decline any first-declension feminine noun ending in -η in all five cases and both numbers.
Recognize the genitive singular ending -ης and the dative singular -ῃ.
Distinguish first-declension feminines from second-declension masculines by their endings.
Parse first-declension feminine nouns in -η on sight.

sections.heading: The first declension
sections.body:
The first declension contains most feminine nouns. It has three sub-types depending on the vowel in the stem: nouns in -η, nouns in -α (long), and nouns in -α (short). Today we take the first type: feminines ending in -η.

These nouns are regular. The nominative singular ends in -η, the genitive singular in -ης, the dative singular in -ῃ (with iota subscript), the accusative singular in -ην. The plural endings are the same for all three sub-types of the first declension.

sections.heading: The paradigm: ἡ ἀρετή (excellence, virtue)
sections.body:
singular        plural
  nominative  ἀρετή           ἀρεταί
  genitive    ἀρετῆς          ἀρετῶν
  dative      ἀρετῇ           ἀρεταῖς
  accusative  ἀρετήν          ἀρετάς
  vocative    ἀρετή           ἀρεταί

With the article:
  nominative  ἡ ἀρετή         αἱ ἀρεταί
  genitive    τῆς ἀρετῆς      τῶν ἀρετῶν
  dative      τῇ ἀρετῇ        ταῖς ἀρεταῖς
  accusative  τὴν ἀρετήν      τὰς ἀρετάς
  vocative    ὦ ἀρετή         ὦ ἀρεταί

The genitive and dative singular have a circumflex on the ultima: -ῆς, -ῇ. This is regular and predictable.
